name_note: GTDB splits the classical species Streptococcus salivarius into several species, so s__Streptococcus salivarius_D is narrower than the name used in papers; its genomes are named Streptococcus salivarius in NCBI.

sentences.text: Streptococcus salivarius is a gram-positive viridans group streptococcus described as a benign commensal that primarily colonizes the oral cavity and the gastrointestinal tract.

In 44 healthy and stunted children from Bangui, Central African Republic, saliva showed higher Streptococcus salivarius nucleotide diversity than other compartments, consistent with frequent translocation from the mouth to the lower gut.

In that study, 87 Streptococcus salivarius isolates were whole-genome sequenced, and fecal isolates were more closely related to oral isolates from the same individuals than to those from other individuals.

An analysis of 1,644 paired oral and fecal metagenomes reported that 74.5% of cases of species detected at both sites involved the same strains, primarily abundant oral species such as Streptococcus salivarius.
Invasive infections with this species have been reported, typically in immunocompromised hosts or following invasive gastrointestinal or spinal procedures.
